pātimokkha: [ pa + atimokkha ] (na) CL=7 pātimokkha 1Pātimokkha  (A) The greatest virtue. (b) The book that explains or points out the greatest virtues/precepts that is called pātimokkha.

[ pāti + mokkha ]  CL=7 Precepts for Buddhist Monastics (Pātimokkha): (A) The precepts that protect from the suffering of lower realms (Āpāyikadukkha), benefiting the preceptors. (B) The precepts that liberate beings in saṃsāra from defilements (saṃkilesa) such as craving, which originate in ignorance (Avijjā). (C) The precepts that liberate the mind from suffering. (D) The precepts that enable liberation from defilements (such as craving), which lead to suffering in saṃsāra. (E) The precepts that cause liberation from attachment to the six sense bases (Āyatana). (F) The precepts that free ordinary beings (puthujjana) who fall into lower realms from the suffering of saṃsāra. (G) The precepts that liberate the restless, wandering mind from saṃsāric suffering. (H) The precepts that free the mind trapped in the false sense of self, which perpetuates cyclic suffering across realms. (I) The precepts that ultimately liberate beings from the suffering of saṃsāra.

[ pati + mokkha ] (ti) CL=7 A chief of a whole world (A) The virtues of Lord Buddha that is a cause of liberation. (E) The virtues that happen to lead to Nibbāna.

pāḷi: [ pā + ḷi. Moga,7.228. Dhāna,ṭī.539. Pāla + ṇi. Yādicchakanāma. Pa + āḷi. Atthaṃ pāletīti pāḷi, lassa ḷattaṃ. Antodakaṃ rakkhaṇatthena mahato taḷākassa thirā mahatīti pāḷi viyāti pāḷi. Pariyatti-dhammo. Pakaṭṭhānaṃ ukkaṭṭhānaṃ sīlādiatthānaṃ bodhanato sabhāvaniruttibhāvato buddhādīhi bhāsitattā ca pakaṭṭhānaṃ vacanappa-bandhānaṃ aḷīti pāḷi. Pāḷisaddo pāḷidhamme, taḷākapāḷiyampi ca, dissate pantiyañceva, iti ñe yyaṃ vijānatā. Pāṭipadiko hi pantivācako pāḷisaddo. Nīti,dhā.340. ]  CL=9 (1) line, order. (a) the line of the holy words of the Buddha, three baskets of Pāḷi, Pariyattidhamma.  (Either all the Dhamma or one Nikāya or one Sutta or one paragraph or one word, preached by the Buddha, is called 'Pāḷi'. The quotation made by Nīti, dhā, 340 and Nīti, dhā, sya is that Pāḷi is so called because it is similar to a strong and huge embankment of a dam. It makes known the sense of Sīla, etc., which are noble, it is also Sabhāvaniruttti, and it is preached by the Buddha, etc., it is 'the noble word or sound'
